**Analysis summary:**

The test image shows a **field-level view** with irregular patches of yellowing/browning premature plant senescence scattered throughout an otherwise green soybean canopy. This is the classic field presentation of a root/soil-borne disease causing localized plant death.

Comparing against references:
- **Sudden Death Syndrome**: The SDS reference (bottom-right panel) shows essentially identical field-level patchy yellowing/browning in irregular clusters — best match
- **Soybean Cyst Nematode**: Also causes patches but plants tend to be more stunted/chlorotic with less browning; no match to this color pattern
- **Charcoal Rot**: Causes rows of dead plants along soil stress zones, not the irregular scattered patches seen here
- **Septoria/Cercospora/other foliar diseases**: Leaf-level diseases — would show uniform canopy yellowing, not distinct patches
- **Phytophthora/White Mold/Diaporthe**: Individual plant collapse, not large irregular field patches

The irregular patch distribution with yellow-to-orange-brown coloration and mid-to-late season timing is the defining field signature of SDS, where Fusarium virguliforme infects roots in wet areas causing interveinal chlorosis/necrosis in field patches.
